With \(A\) as origin, let \(\vec B=\vec b\), \(\vec C=\vec c\), \(\vec O=\vec o\). From
\[
\vec{AB}+\vec{AC}=2\vec{AO}
\]
we get
\[
\vec b+\vec c=2\vec o \implies \vec o=\frac{\vec b+\vec c}{2}.
\]
So \(O\) is the midpoint of \(BC\).

Since the circumradius is \(2\), \(|\vec o|=|\vec{AO}|=2\), hence
\[
\left|\frac{\vec b+\vec c}{2}\right|=2 \implies |\vec b+\vec c|=4.
\]
Also, since \(B\) lies on the circle centered at \(O\),
\[
|\vec b-\vec o|=2.
\]
But \(\vec b-\vec o=\frac{\vec b-\vec c}{2}\), so
\[
|\vec b-\vec c|=4.
\]
Given \(|\vec b|=|\vec{AB}|=|\vec{AO}|=2\). Now square:
\[
|\vec b+\vec c|^2=16 \implies |\vec b|^2+|\vec c|^2+2\vec b\cdot\vec c=16,
\]
\[
|\vec b-\vec c|^2=16 \implies |\vec b|^2+|\vec c|^2-2\vec b\cdot\vec c=16.
\]
Subtracting gives \(\vec b\cdot\vec c=0\), so
\[
4+|\vec c|^2=16 \implies |\vec c|^2=12.
\]
Thus
\[
\vec{CA}\cdot\vec{CB}=(-\vec c)\cdot(\vec b-\vec c)
=|\vec c|^2-\vec b\cdot\vec c=12.
\]
\[
\boxed{12}
\]
